test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 02 Dec 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All bears are rabbits.

All rabbits are dogs.

Some dogs are black.

**Conclusions.**

I. Some rabbits are black.

II. Some dogs are bears.

III. All bears are dogs.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow.

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f81e3ed4687123bff80c8091c10d7e7d1e6a646f2a69d24b25f08bc383e78aeb.png] 

 

Conclusions:

I. Some rabbits are black → Does not follow (As all rabbits are dogs and some dogs are black. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

II. Some dogs are bears → **F**ollow (As all bears are rabbits and all rabbits are dogs. So, as whole bears comes in dogs therefore it is definitely true)

III. All bears are dogs → Follow (As all bears are rabbits and all rabbits are dogs. So, as whole bears comes in dogs therefore it is definitely true)

∴ Here, Only conclusions II and III follow.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only conclusions II and III follow**".
